error_modes.label: Normal Landing - touchdown point control
error_modes.source: specific:TOUCH DOWN POINT (feet from the beginning of the RWY) [a/ FLAPS LDG - FLAPS T/O - AOA]

texts.0: SP, due to a late and shallow round out flown with residual power, did not bring the A/C to the touchdown point as described in the Flight Manuals. The A/C floated in ground effect and contacted the RWY beyond 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY, outside the landing criteria. The IP took the controls to arrest the float and reposition the A/C. The aim point was neither selected nor protected during the level off.
texts.1: SP, due to a delayed power reduction during the level off, carried excess energy into the flare and extended the float. Touchdown was achieved at the 1500 ft limit from the beginning of the RWY, and only after the IP called for the power to be closed and the landing attitude to be held. SP did not recognize the developing float from the aircraft's response before the verbal prompt.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly high round out, allowed a short float before contact with the RWY. Touchdown occurred between 1000 and 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY. SP recognized the float, held the landing attitude and completed the touchdown in time, without any intervention from the IP.
texts.3: SP executed the round out timely, levelled off the A/C, assumed the landing attitude and brought the A/C in touch with the RWY as described in the Flight Manuals. Touchdown was achieved within 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, on the selected aim point. The gradual power reduction and the control of the rate of descent were consistent throughout the level off.
texts.4: SP flew the round out and the flare with precise power and attitude control, placing the A/C on the selected aim point with negligible dispersion between repeated landings. Touchdown was achieved comfortably within 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, with no float and no late correction. Aim point discipline was maintained from the final part of the approach to contact.
texts.marginal: SP touched down within the required 1000 ft from the beginning of the RWY, but consistently at the far end of that band. The tendency is a round out started slightly high, which produces a brief float before contact and moves the touchdown point long. SP is expected to begin the gradual power reduction earlier and to hold the landing attitude with less float, so that the touchdown point is centred on the aim point rather than at the limit.

texts_at.0: SP flew the round out and flare with the IP calling for the gradual power reduction to begin before the float can start, since bringing the aircraft to the touchdown point without that call has not yet been practiced. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to begin the power reduction independently before the float can start.
texts_at.1: SP brought the A/C to the touchdown point as described in the Flight Manuals, holding contact to approximately 1450 ft from the beginning of the RWY, at the outer edge of the standard, due to the gradual power reduction during the level off being confirmed only after the float had already started rather than before it. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to confirm the power reduction before the float can start rather than once it has already begun.
texts_at.2: SP achieved touchdown at about 1300 ft from the beginning of the RWY, due to the landing attitude being held a beat longer than the technique calls for before the rate of descent was allowed to resume. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to allow the rate of descent to resume as soon as the landing attitude is confirmed rather than holding it a beat longer.
texts_at.3: SP executed the round out timely and brought the A/C in touch with the RWY within approximately 900 ft from the beginning of the RWY, due to the control of the rate of descent through the level off being a fraction less continuous than the technique calls for. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to keep the rate-of-descent control continuous through the whole level off.

texts_above.1: SP brought the A/C to the touchdown point as described in the Flight Manuals, holding contact to approximately 1450 ft from the beginning of the RWY after the power reduction was called before the float. texts_above.2: SP executed the round out timely on every landing and controlled the rate of descent through the level off, placing touchdown at about 1250 ft from the beginning of the RWY with the gradual power reduction consistent throughout. error_modes.source: specific:DEVIATION FROM CENTER LINE (feet) [a/ FLAPS LDG - FLAPS T/O - AOA]|general:a,f

texts.0: SP, due to uncorrected drift in the last seconds of the approach, did not direct the A/C to the RWY centerline before contact. texts.1: SP, due to a late rudder input during the alignment, allowed the A/C to displace laterally from the extended centerline during the round out. Touchdown occurred at 15 ft from the centerline, and the correction was applied only after the IP called for it. SP did not detect the lateral displacement from the outside references before contact.
texts.2: SP, due to a slow initial alignment with the RWY, developed a lateral displacement during the round out. Touchdown occurred between 5 and 15 ft from the centerline. SP recognized the displacement in time, applied coordinated rudder and aileron to direct the A/C back to the centerline and completed the landing without intervention from the IP.
texts.3: SP directed the A/C to the RWY centerline in the final part of the approach and held the alignment throughout the round out. Touchdown occurred within 5 ft of the centerline, with the longitudinal axis aligned with the RWY and no drift. Directional control was maintained through the initial deceleration.
texts.4: SP held the A/C on the RWY centerline with negligible lateral displacement through the round out, the flare and the touchdown. Contact was made on the centerline with the longitudinal axis aligned and no drift, and the alignment was maintained through the rollout. No visible corrective input was required in the last part of the approach.

The tendency is a rudder input applied slightly late in the alignment, which leaves a small residual displacement at contact. SP is expected to establish the centerline alignment earlier in the round out so that touchdown is centred on the RWY rather than offset within the tolerance.

texts.0: SP, due to an incorrect application of the standard deceleration procedure, did not decelerate the A/C to a safe taxi speed and did not follow the LAPs when vacating the RWY. Braking was uneven and produced abrupt lateral oscillations along the RWY, and the turn-off was attempted above safe taxi speed. The IP took the controls to control the A/C and to vacate the RWY.
texts.1: SP, due to braking applied late and asymmetrically after touchdown, allowed the A/C to oscillate laterally during the deceleration. The deceleration was brought back to the standard procedure and the correct taxiway was taken only after the IP directed it. SP did not recognize the excess turn-off speed unprompted.
texts.2: SP, due to a late start of the deceleration after touchdown, approached the intended turn-off above the planned speed. SP recognized the situation, applied the standard braking procedure without abrupt inputs, reduced the A/C to a safe taxi speed and vacated the RWY following the LAPs, without any intervention from the IP.
texts.3: SP decelerated the A/C to taxi speed after touchdown by applying the standard procedure, without abrupt oscillations, and vacated the RWY following the LAPs with no deviations. Directional control was maintained on the centerline throughout the rollout. The turn-off was made at a safe taxi speed at the planned taxiway.
texts.4: SP controlled the rollout with smooth, symmetrical braking and precise directional control, keeping the A/C on the centerline with no oscillation at any speed. texts.marginal: SP decelerated the A/C by the standard procedure and vacated the RWY following the LAPs, but the braking was consistently applied later than planned. The tendency is a rollout that arrives at the turn-off with little margin, requiring a firmer final brake application. SP is expected to start the deceleration earlier so that safe taxi speed is established well before the taxiway.

error_modes.label: Recognition of abnormal landing conditions and go-around decision

texts.0: SP, due to continuation bias in pressing the landing after the touchdown parameters were clearly no longer achievable, did not recognize the developing porpoising and did not react as required. The approach was continued to a contact outside the landing criteria instead of the go-around demanded by the conditions. The IP took the controls, terminated the landing and executed the go-around.

The go-around was executed only after the IP directed it, and the A/C was already outside the touchdown parameters at that point. SP recognized the abnormal condition but did not translate the recognition into a decision.
texts.2: SP, due to a delayed assessment of the developing float, held the landing longer than the conditions supported. SP then recognized that the touchdown parameters could still be met, corrected the attitude and the power and completed the landing within the criteria without any intervention from the IP. texts.3: SP prevented and recognized the conditions that lead to high flare, late or rapid round out, porpoising, floating, ballooning, bouncing and touchdown with drift, and reacted accordingly. Where the crosswind controls were not adequate and the touchdown parameters were not met, SP executed the go-around without hesitation. The decision was made early and announced clearly.
texts.4: SP anticipated the conditions that produce an abnormal landing and corrected them before they developed, so that no float, balloon, bounce or drift at contact appeared. Where a go-around was required, the decision was taken at the earliest recognizable point and executed by the standard procedure. The reasoning behind each decision was stated to the IP as the situation developed.
texts.marginal: SP recognized the abnormal landing conditions and reacted correctly, but the decision to go around was consistently taken later than the situation allowed. error_modes.label: High flare recognition and backpressure release recovery

texts.0: SP, due to a round out executed too early and with excessive pitch up, did not release backpressure to increase the descent rate as the high flare developed. The A/C was held above the normal flare height until the airspeed decayed and it then dropped onto the RWY beyond 1900 feet from the beginning of the RWY, with the nose close to premature gear contact. The IP took the controls, applied power and arrested the sink rate.
texts.1: SP, due to a flare begun too high above the RWY and with excessive pitch up, did not release a small amount of backpressure to re-establish the normal descent rate. The A/C settled from the high flare with a marked sink rate and touched down at the 1500 feet limit from the beginning of the RWY, 10 knots above the touchdown speed. SP corrected the pitch only after the IP called the high flare.
texts.2: SP, due to a round out started slightly early, levelled off above the normal flare height. SP recognized the high flare without prompting, released a small amount of backpressure to increase the descent rate and increased backpressure again as the A/C approached normal altitude. The landing was completed about 1300 feet from the beginning of the RWY with no hard contact and no radical pitch change.
texts.3: SP began the round out at the correct height and controlled the pitch so that the flare was established at normal altitude. Where the A/C levelled off slightly high, SP released a small amount of backpressure and re-established the normal flare with adequate airspeed and RWY remaining. Contact occurred within 1000 feet from the beginning of the RWY, in the landing attitude described in the Flight Manuals.
texts.4: SP judged the flare height against the outside references on every landing, so no high flare developed and no corrective release of backpressure was required. Pitch was applied progressively at a rate proportional to the rate of descent, with touchdown well inside 1000 feet from the beginning of the RWY. Where the airspeed or the RWY remaining would not have supported a recovery, SP stated the go-around decision in advance.
texts.marginal: SP kept the flare height and the touchdown point within the standards, but consistently levelled off a little higher than normal and had to release backpressure to re-establish the descent. The tendency is a round out started early, which leaves less airspeed margin at the point where the landing attitude is attained. SP is expected to delay the round out to the correct height so that the flare needs no corrective release of backpressure.

texts_at.0: SP flared the aircraft with the IP calling for the small backpressure release to be applied as the high flare first appears, since recognizing the flare height against the outside references without that call has not yet been practiced. The A/C reached the landing attitude with a descent rate well above normal and contacted the RWY heavily, outside the landing criteria and with the pitch still increasing. The IP held the landing attitude and rapidly advanced the PCL to MAX to recover the A/C.
texts.1: SP, due to a higher than expected descent rate recognized late, did not complete the flare in the time available and rounded out rapidly just before contact. The touchdown was firm, at the 1500 feet limit from the beginning of the RWY and 10 knots above the touchdown speed, with the landing attitude reached only at the moment of contact. SP held the attitude and added power after the IP called for it.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly late recognition of the sink rate, began the round out later than planned. SP increased backpressure at a rate proportional to the rate of descent, held the landing attitude and added the power required, so the contact remained moderate about 1250 feet from the beginning of the RWY. No abrupt round out and no intervention from the IP were needed.
texts.3: SP judged the altitude and the descent rate correctly and executed the round out timely, so the flare was completed before the landing attitude was required. Backpressure was applied at a rate proportional to the rate of descent and the A/C was brought in touch with the RWY within 1000 feet from the beginning of the RWY. No abrupt pitch input was needed to prevent premature contact.
texts.4: SP matched the rate of backpressure to the rate of descent on every landing, so that no late or rapid round out appeared even where the sink rate was higher than briefed. Touchdowns were consistently smooth and well inside the touchdown parameters, with no tendency towards an accelerated stall in the flare. SP stated in advance that a late round out would be answered by holding the landing attitude and advancing the PCL to MAX.
texts.marginal: SP completed the round out within the standards, but the level off was consistently initiated late and finished with a faster than normal application of backpressure. The tendency is a height judgement taken from the instruments rather than from the outside references, which leaves little time to complete the flare. SP is expected to start the round out at the briefed height so the pitch rate stays proportional to the rate of descent.

texts_at.0: SP judged the round out with the IP calling the sink rate as it first began to build, since recognizing that trend before it becomes pronounced has not yet been practiced without that call. error_modes.label: Porpoising - nose gear contact before the main gear and oscillation damping

texts.0: SP, due to an incorrect landing attitude combined with excess airspeed at contact, did not attain the landing attitude before touchdown and the nose gear contacted the RWY before the main gear. SP then attempted to counteract each bounce with opposite control stick movement, which aggravated the oscillation into a developing porpoise with repeated heavy contacts. The IP took the controls, set the takeoff attitude and advanced the PCL to MAX.
texts.1: SP, due to a nose low landing attitude carried into the contact at a speed 10 knots above the touchdown speed, did not prevent the nose gear from touching almost together with the main gear. A short pitch oscillation followed and was stopped only when the IP called for the takeoff attitude and MAX power. SP then held the controls steady in the recovery position and did not raise the landing gear.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly nose low attitude at the beginning of the flare, allowed the pitch to decrease as the A/C settled. SP recognized the attitude before contact, increased backpressure so the main gear touched first and held the controls steady, so no pitch oscillation developed. The touchdown occurred about 1200 feet from the beginning of the RWY at 7 knots above the touchdown speed.
texts.3: SP brought the A/C in touch with the RWY in the landing attitude described in the Flight Manuals, with the main gear contacting first and the nose gear lowered afterwards. Speed at contact stayed within 5 knots of the touchdown speed and no pitch oscillation appeared. Backstick pressure was relaxed slowly and the nose gear was lowered smoothly to the RWY.
texts.4: SP controlled attitude and airspeed so precisely that every contact was made on the main gear with the nose clearly high and the PCL at idle. No tendency to porpoise appeared on any landing, and the nose gear was lowered progressively after the main gear was firmly on the RWY. SP briefed the recovery in advance: takeoff attitude, PCL to MAX, controls held steady and gear left down.
texts.marginal: SP touched down on the main gear within the standards, but the landing attitude was consistently flatter than described in the Flight Manuals and the nose gear was lowered very early. The tendency leaves little margin between main gear and nose gear contact, which is the condition that produces a porpoise. SP is expected to hold the landing attitude after contact and to relax backstick pressure slowly before lowering the nose gear.

The IP took the controls and executed the go-around.

SP increased the pitch attitude and accepted the landing only after the IP pointed out the float.

The flap setting selected matched the landing distance and the wind, and prolonged floating in the crosswind was avoided entirely. SP stated the point beyond which a long landing would be accepted as inevitable and a go-around flown.

SP is expected to complete the power reduction on schedule so that the A/C arrives at the flare on speed.

texts.4: SP flew the AOA landing with the transition from the indexer to the runway picture made at the round out without a glance back, the landing attitude assumed on time and the touchdown within a few knots of the target on the main gear. Nothing in the technique needed a correction.

error_modes.label: Bounce: firm touchdown before the landing attitude, and the continue-or-go-around decision

texts.0: SP, due to a late recognition that the aircraft was settling fast combined with excessive back stick pressure, touched down firmly before the landing attitude was attained and bounced with the aircraft rising rapidly. SP attempted to land from the severe bounce instead of going around, with the result that the second touchdown was harder than the first and beyond 1500 ft from the beginning of the RWY. The IP took the controls and flew the go-around.
